qa_history.question: Is the crown likely original given only one photo is available?
qa_history.answer:
Honestly, I can't make a reliable call on crown originality from this image. The single on-wrist photo shows the dial and case front reasonably well, but the crown itself is largely obscured/out of frame at this angle - I can't even confirm its shape, logo, or signing.

For what it's worth on Constellation 168.027 pieces, the correct crown is typically a signed Omega crown (often with the Constellation "C" logo or Omega symbol embossed), sometimes with a small dot or "Ω" motif depending on production year. Replacement crowns are common on vintage pieces that have seen service work, and unsigned or generic crowns are a frequent giveaway of a swap - but none of that can be verified here.

To actually assess this, you'd need:
- A close-up photo of the crown itself (logo, shape, fluting pattern)
- Ideally a shot showing the crown from the side to check tube fit/proportions

Without that, I'd treat crown originality as unconfirmed/unknown rather than assume it's fine - worth asking the seller directly for a macro shot before paying $1,399, especially since your authenticity risk is already medium due to the lack of movement/case-back photos.

Based on the listing title, the seller states it's a Cal. 564 - Omega's automatic movement used in Constellation models during the mid-to-late 1960s. This is consistent with the 168.027 reference, as that case/dial combination was indeed paired with the 24-jewel Cal. 564 (part of Omega's 560-family, chronometer-grade) in period-correct production.

That said, a couple of caveats:

- This is only stated in the title text - there's no photo of the movement itself (through a case-back or open case) to confirm the caliber is actually present and matches.
- I can't verify from the single wrist photo whether the movement is original to the watch or a later service replacement, whether it's been re-signed, or whether it carries a proper chronometer certification stamp (168.027 examples often came in chronometer-rated versions, which affects value).

If confirming movement authenticity matters to you at this price point, ask the seller for a case-back photo and, ideally, a shot of the movement itself with the caliber number and serial visible.

This Omega Constellation 168.005 watch art print captures the elegant lines and refined proportions of the iconic "Pie Pan" model in meticulous technical detail. The sketch reveals the silvery dial, faceted bezel, and integrated bracelet with precision dimension annotations, rendered in clean pencil-sketch style against a soft neutral background. Every detail of this legendary automatic timepiece is preserved with draftsman clarity.

The blueprint-inspired aesthetic brings sophisticated horology charm to a study, office, man cave, or bedroom. It's ideal for watch collectors who own or admire this reference, adding a gallery-worthy tribute to their favorite wristwatch. The matte finish and museum-quality paper give it a refined, professional look that fits beautifully in modern or classic interiors.

This print celebrates craftsmanship and precision, making it a thoughtful anniversary gift, groomsmen present, retirement keepsake, or birthday surprise for the watch enthusiast in your life.

Details:
• Giclée fine-art print produced with 12-color archival ink for vivid, true-to-life color depth that goes beyond standard 4-color inkjet
• Smooth matte finish for a clean, glare-free display
• Premium archival-grade museum paper, 200 gsm
• Frame not included
• Available in multiple sizes to fit any space or standard frame
• Printed on FSC-certified, eco-friendly paper

Please note: Colors and positioning may vary slightly depending on your screen settings and print production.

Powered by Omega's reliable Swiss quartz movement, this version offers exceptional accuracy, low maintenance, and the slim wearing profile that many enthusiasts prefer. Original examples from the early 2000s continue to be sought after as modern classics within the Omega collection.

listing.title: Omega Seamaster Ref. 2635 “Hammer” Automatic, Swiss 1952
listing.body:
Rare, Beautiful and Iconic ** Early Vintage Omega Seamaster Ref. 2635 “Hammer” Automatic, Swiss 1952 **

Launched in 1948 to concur with Omega’s Centennial celebrations, the Seamaster line issued as a civilian version inspired by the waterproof wristwatches Omega had produced for the British military in the latter part of WWII. The new design concept was: “A robust yet elegant watch for active individuals who want a watch for “town, sea and country”.

All the early Seamaster watches were equipped with self-winding movements, and rapidly found favor in the marketplace for their robustness, accuracy and reliability. 

Moreover, in those days water-resistant watches generally had lead or shellac gaskets to hermetically seal the watch case… and these were susceptible leakage resulting from temperature changes… the Seamaster watchcase was sealed with a rubber O-ring gasket of the type that had proven its abilities in submarines during the Second World War. Thus, in 1955 the Seamaster achieved its first diving-record, when Australian Gordon McLean wore one to the depth of 62.5 meters.

Additionally, the Seamaster was independently tested by the Swiss Laboratory for Watch Research which subjected 50 cases to tests at a simulated depth of 60 meters. After temperature changes of -40° C to 50° C in quick succession, the cases showed no sign of water infiltration. In fact, the engineers at OMEGA were so confident of the Seamaster that one flew the Polar Route over the North Atlantic in 1956… attached to the outside of a Douglas DC6 aircraft!

The Omega Seamaster also is Iconic for its role as the trusted watch of 007 agent James Bond… Of which the Semaster Ref. 2635, presently offered here for your consideration, is the venerable grandfather! 

Material: Stainless Steel 
Dial: Silvered with Applied Numerals and Shark -Tooth Batons, Fully Original
Bracelet: Black Crocodile 
Buckle: Omega, Stainless steel 
Movement: Omega Calibre 354, “Hammer” Automatic Self-Winding 
Case: 32.5 mm diameter (excluding the winder crown) x 40 mm Length (lug-to-lug)
Condition: Excellent, Fully Serviced by Master Swiss Watchmaker.

Shipping: Worldwide; Duty-Free Shipping within Europe




OMEGA Watch Company
The Omega Watch Company was founded by Louis Brandt in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, in 1848. Initially the firm assembled key-wound precision pocket watches using parts supplied by local craftsmen. 

After Louis Brandt's death in 1879, his two sons Louis-Paul and Cesar took over control of the business. Louis-Paul and César Brandt both died in 1903, leaving one of Switzerland's largest watch companies - with an annual production of 240,000 watches and 800 employees - in the hands of four young Brandt family members, the oldest of whom was Paul-Emile Brandt. 

The difficult economic times that followed World War I caused Paul-Emil Brandt, as of 1925, to actively seek a union between OMEGA and Tissot… then subsequently their merger in 1930 within the group SSIH. 

By the 1970s, SSIH had become Switzerland's no 1 producer of finished watches; however, due to the severe monetary crisis and recession of 1975 through 1980, in 1981 SSIH had to be bailed out by the banks.. so that in 1985 the holding company was taken over by a group of private investors and renamed SMH, Societe suisse de microelectronique et d'horlogerie.

The new group achieved rapid growth and success to become today's top watch producer in the world. Named Swatch Group in 1998, it now notably includes Blancpain and Breguet. 

Dynamic and flourishing, OMEGA remains one of its most prestigious flagship brands.
